subject: DryDock on-prem constraints, nodepool design & DR runbook
messages:
From: Aylin Kaya <aylin@drydock.co>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DryDock on-prem constraints + ask: nodepool sizing and DR

Hiro / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We've pulled together the site constraints and need Redwood's recommendation on two things before we lock the SOW:

1) Nodepool mix given constrained rack power (two 20A PDUs per rack, expected 6 racks). Most nodes will be dual-socket 32-core with 4 x 3.84TB NVMe each; we can also attach a small number of 8x A100-style GPU hosts (we're aiming for burst inference).
2) A practical DR runbook: acceptable RTO is 2 hours for inference endpoints and 6 hours for batch replays; we need a documented failover path that doesn't rely on synchronous block replication across sites.

Attached is the network diagram and a draft milestone sheet (links below). Can Redwood propose a preferred nodepool layout, PV class choices, and a short DR flow we can include in the architecture appendix? Also flag any blockers for on-prem private control plane (we have an air-gapped VLAN available for control plane traffic).

Appreciate a short write-up by Monday (9th) so we can fold into procurement.

Regards,
Aylin
Head of Infrastructure
DryDock Logistics

Thanks Aylin — good context. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short one-page proposal and a runbook draft first thing Monday. Quick notes now so your procurement team can see the blocking items: 

- Nodepools: propose 3 pools
  * control-plane hosts (2-3 redundant VMs on separate racks, air-gapped control VLAN; lightweight - 8 cores, 64GB, mirrored SSDs)
  * inference GPUs (N = 6 burst-capable hosts, isolated to a GPU pool, each with 8 TB local NVMe for model cache; consider single-socket 64GB memory node if budget constrained)
  * general-purpose stateless workers (autoscaling; dual-socket 32-core; 384GB RAM; local NVMe for temp caches)

- PV classes: use two classes
  * fast-local-nvme (local-storage CSI with read-mostly caching for model shard temporary storage)
  * replicated-block (Ceph/Rook or external SAN for training artifacts, logs that must be durable)

- DR strategy (short):
  * Active site primary; warm standby in another colo (cold-cache approach): model artifacts in replicated-block; model caches repopulated on failover. 
  * For endpoints: maintain DNS TTL 60s + load-balancer health checks and a small fleet of hot-standby inference nodes (fractional reserved GPUs) that can absorb traffic during failover. 

Blockers:
- No synchronous geo-replication for NVMe local caches; this is fine if we accept cache warm-up.
- Control-plane air-gapped VLAN: Redwood Private control plane needs outbound connectivity for license checks (we can work with an intermittent egress appliance or offline token).

I'll attach a compact diagram and Milestones tracker Monday AM.

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Hi Aylin —

Attached is the 1-page proposal and the DR runbook draft you asked for. Highlights:

- Recommended node counts (initial):
  * GPU inference: 6 nodes (each with 4 x A100 equiv) — supports steady 800 reqs/s with burst headroom; suggest 2 reserved for hot-standby
  * Statless workers: start with 12 dual-socket nodes, HPA to 24 for batch jobs
  * Control plane: 3 VMs across racks for quorum + single-node fallback mode documented

- Storage:
  * fast-local-nvme for model caches (CSI local PV) — ephemeral, repopulate from replicated-block after failover
  * replicated-block (Rook/Ceph) on 3-node archive pool — for artifacts + audit logs; expectation: ~200TB usable

- DR runbook (summary):
  1) Detect: LB health or loss of majority in control plane -> page SRE
  2) Promote standby: DNS failover to warm site + bootstrap small GPU pool from replicated-block
  3) Rehydrate caches: parallel model pull with rate-limited concurrency to avoid egress saturation
  4) Postmortem: capture cache TTLs, eviction patterns, recommend increasing hot-reserve if needed

Blockers and open items:
- Procurement needs to confirm power budget per rack and whether GPU hosts can be concentrated or must be spread for cooling.
- DryDock to confirm whether RTO target for batch (6h) can accept full replay from replicated-block if no snapshot exists.

I've left comments in the milestones sheet for expected procurement windows. If that looks good, Hiro and I can convert this into an appendix for the SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Hiro —

This looks great and aligns with the internal checklist. A couple of quick clarifications before we sign: 

1) For the replicated-block, do you expect Rook/Ceph to be managed by Redwood as part of Private, or do we need to add a vendor-managed SAN? Cost delta will drive our decision.
2) Can you add an explicit step in the DR runbook for failback sequencing (we want to avoid double-writes during rehydrate)?

If you can drop a single paragraph for each point into the appendix, we can greenlight and push the SOW to legal.

Thanks — Marcus
VP Engineering, DryDock Logistics
